newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish public will sway EMU decision - FinMin.
newsitem.headline: Swedish public will sway EMU decision - FinMin.

text.p: Public opinion in autumn 1997 will determine if Sweden will enter Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999, Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said in a speech on Wednesday.
"We cannot take a decision on this question that is contrary to the Swedish public wishes," Asbrink said.
"If there is an opinion against EMU in autumn 1997 the conclusion must be that we do not go in, at any rate not at the earliest occasion."
Sweden will manage in either situation, Asbrink said.
"We have the freedom to say yes or no and we can live with both alternatives," he said.
Sweden's ruling Social Democrat party is expected to make a decision on whether Sweden will enter EMU at its party congress in autumn next year.
To date public opinion has weighed against membership but a poll released on Wednesday showed that more Swedes were in favour of EMU than previously thought.
The poll by SIFO, the Swedish Institute for Public Opinion Research, found that 44 percent of those polled were positive towards Swedish membership of EMU while 40 percent were opposed.
An earlier poll of 1,000 Swedes published on November 7 showed that 54 percent would say no to EMU if a referendum were held at the time of the survey and only 21 percent would vote to join.
